codeFindings.title: Submit only displays an unverified success message
codeFindings.detail: The submit handler only adds the modal class; it neither sends the counted values nor persists them anywhere, despite claiming the audit was recorded.
codeFindings.notVerifiableBecause: The UI always shows the same success dialog and exposes no rendered result proving whether counts were recorded or sent to a backend.

results.intentUsed:
Exercise every audit control, probe count boundaries and per-row variance updates, verify reset behavior, and test all dialog closing methods.

Work through these checks in order, and record what you actually observe for each:
1. Use the Panel A3 row, which starts at counted 7. Then Click its minus stepper eight times and read the counted value and variance. — expect: Count must stop at 0 and variance must remain -7; state both values.
2. Note all four initial rows and their counts and variances. Then Click plus twice for Washer 11mm and minus once for Cable 2m. — expect: Washer must read 62 and +2; Cable must read 17 and -1; other rows must remain unchanged.
3. Change Hex bolt M4 and Panel A3 to distinct non-system counts. Then Click Reset counts and reread every row. — expect: Every counted value must equal its System value and every variance must show —.
4. Change at least one item count so the audit has a visible nonzero variance. Then Click Submit audit. — expect: A visible dialog must show “Audit submitted” and the recording confirmation message.
5. Open the submission dialog. Then Close it with Close, reopen it, click outside, reopen it, then press Escape. — expect: The dialog must disappear after each of the three closing methods.
6. Set the viewport to a narrow mobile width and open the submission dialog. Then Inspect the table, dialog text, and all stepper and dialog buttons at that width. — expect: All text and controls must remain legible, reachable, and unclipped

verifications.claim: The audit table and every stepper/bottom action remain readable and reachable at a narrow mobile viewport without clipping.
verifications.evidence: The trace contains no viewport resize to a narrow width and no recorded inspection of clipping, readability, or reachability at mobile dimensions.

verifications.claim: Submitting an audit opens the “Audit submitted” modal, and the Close button visibly dismisses it.
verifications.evidence: After Submit audit, step 14 observed a visible “Audit submitted” modal with a dimmed background; after Close, step 15 observed that the modal disappeared and the undimmed table remained visible.

verifications.claim: The submission modal can be dismissed with Escape.
verifications.evidence: Step 16 pressed Escape, and step 17 explicitly observed that the dialog remained open after Escape.

verifications.claim: The submission modal can be dismissed by clicking outside it.
verifications.evidence: Step 17 clicked empty backdrop space outside the dialog, and step 18 observed that the click closed the dialog while the table remained visible.

verifications.claim: Reset counts restores every row’s counted value to its System value and shows an em dash for every variance.
verifications.evidence: Steps 9, 11, 19, 21, 23, and 26 each observed Reset counts restoring Hex 140, Washer 60, Cable 18, and Panel A3 7 with em-dash variances for all rows.

verifications.claim: Decreasing Washer 11mm twice and increasing Cable 2m twice produces Washer 59/-1 and Cable 20/+2 without changing other rows.
verifications.evidence: The required Cable increments were not performed, and repeated attempted Washer-minus clicks visibly changed Hex instead of Washer (steps 20, 22, 24, and 25), so the Washer interaction needs repeating with a reliable target.
